title: CI workflow: typecheck + tests gate on pull requests
detail: Add .github/workflows/ci.yml: on pull_request → setup pnpm, pnpm install, pnpm --filter @crew/shared build, pnpm typecheck, pnpm test. No publish steps, target <5 min.
rationale: There is no automated gate anywhere: 350 tests + 4 typechecks run only when whoever touches the repo remembers to run them. A PR (watcher PR 1 is next) can reach Navid's merge moment with no evidence its tip still passes. One file, purely mechanical.
outcome: No code needed: Navid landed .github/workflows/ci.yml with today's open-source setup (before this item was picked up) and it is a superset of the spec — on: pull_request + push to main + workflow_dispatch, pnpm 10.17.0 frozen-lockfile install, @crew/shared build, typecheck, tests, plus scripts/smoke.mjs and a cancel-in-progress concurrency group. Verified on origin: latest CI run on main tip 1cb898c is green in 1m05s. Backlog was stale, repo was not.

title: Versioned schema migrations in db.ts (PRAGMA user_version)
detail: packages/supervisor/src/db.ts:47-48 applies schema changes as ad-hoc per-column guards (PRAGMA table_info("channels") then ALTER TABLE). Introduce PRAGMA user_version plus an ordered migrations array executed in one transaction at open; move the existing channels guard into it. Future column/table changes become numbered migrations.
rationale: Every schema change to an existing table is one forgotten table_info guard away from failing boot on every existing install — including live user data dirs. Nothing enforces the guard pattern; a versioned list makes schema changes obvious and idempotent.
outcome: Versioned schema migrations (PRAGMA user_version) landed as eb8d572 on fix/db-migrations: MIGRATIONS list with {name, apply} entries, applied in one transaction on open, version stamped in the same transaction. Sina reviewed and approved with evidence (409/409 tests, typecheck clean, failure-mode checks on legacy db, fresh db, mid-migration crash). One non-blocking nit (sqlite handle leak on failed migrate) filed as its own backlog item. Branch stays local on fix/db-migrations per Mina's spec; promotion to origin/main is Mina's call. 7e223a5 on the branch is Navid's .standbye team-state commit, no code delta.

title: Unit tests for the renderer store: draft lifecycle, reconnect, retry
detail: apps/desktop/src/renderer/state/store.ts (362 lines) is all client logic with zero tests: draft merge from message.draft (store.ts:152-156), message.created clearing (:149-150), supervisor.reconnected → refreshAll (:143), retryMessage (:233). Add vitest to apps/desktop, mock the transport (no electron), and pin: done:true draft replaces growing text; empty done:true clears the draft; events for unknown channels don't crash; reconnect triggers refreshAll; failed send is retryable. Build shared types first.
rationale: The stuck-"writing…" draft bug fixed in 2d8c5c2 was exactly this class of bug — the renderer half of it is unpinned; all 350 tests are supervisor-side. The next event-shape change regresses silently and only surfaces as visual glitches in manual GUI runs.

title: Per-run diff view in the Runs screen
detail: Record the workspace HEAD at run start (one rev-parse where the run's steps are opened) and add a run.diff(runId) hub method returning `git diff <base>..HEAD --stat` plus the patch for the run's workspace. Desktop: a diff tab in the Runs screen rendering the stat with collapsible patches. Fall back to "diff unavailable" if the agent switched branches or rebased mid-run.
rationale: Agents edit files around the clock, but reviewing what a run actually changed requires leaving the app and running git by hand. The owner auditing a night of agent work has no in-app view of a run's file changes today.

title: Message search (FTS5) for the desktop and the agents
detail: packages/supervisor/src/db.ts: FTS5 virtual table over messages kept in sync on insert; hub method messages.search(q, {channelId, agentId, since}); desktop: search field in Inbox/Channel screens; plus a search_messages team tool so agents query history instead of re-reading channels into context.
rationale: Finding what an agent said yesterday means scrolling channel history or querying sqlite by hand. Agents compensate by re-reading whole channels on check-ins, which costs tokens on every run.

title: Close sqlite handle when a migration fails in db.ts open()
detail: In eb8d572 (fix/db-migrations, packages/supervisor/src/db.ts), migrate() runs this.sqlite.transaction(...) and lets a failing migration propagate out of open(). The transaction rolls back correctly, but the better-sqlite3 Database handle is never closed: the caller never receives the object, so the fd and the db lock leak for the life of the process. Fix: wrap the migrate()/open() body in try/catch, call this.sqlite.close() before rethrowing. Test in packages/supervisor/test/db-migrations.test.mjs: a MIGRATIONS entry that throws -> open() rejects AND the underlying file is unlocked (e.g. a second Database open on the same file succeeds). Needs the migrations code from fix/db-migrations, so pick it up on that branch or after it merges to main.
rationale: Every failed migration leaks an open sqlite fd and lock until the supervisor process dies; on a corrupt-schema boot loop that is one leaked handle per boot. Graded non-blocking by Sina in the Mexno2W8 review but it is a real defect on an error path.
